cards.front: First medication to give (chewed) for suspected MI?
cards.back: Aspirin
cards.rationale: Chewed aspirin is given early to inhibit platelets; part of MONA.

cards.back: Sit down; take 1 tab, repeat every 5 min up to 3; call 911 if unrelieved after the first
cards.rationale: NTG dilates vessels and drops BP — sitting prevents falls.

cards.front: Weight gain to report in heart failure?
cards.back: 2–3 lb in a day (or ~5 lb in a week)
cards.rationale: Sudden gain signals fluid retention and worsening HF.

cards.front: Left- vs right-sided HF — where does fluid back up?
cards.back: Left → Lungs (crackles, dyspnea); Right → Rest of body (edema, JVD, ascites)
cards.rationale: “Left = Lungs, Right = Rest of body.”

cards.front: Main risk of atrial fibrillation + prevention?
cards.back: Clot → stroke; prevent with anticoagulation
cards.rationale: Blood pools in the fibrillating atria and forms clots.

cards.front: Signs of DVT — and what NOT to do?
cards.back: Unilateral calf swelling, warmth, redness; do NOT massage the leg
cards.rationale: Massage can dislodge the clot into a pulmonary embolism.

cards.back: Hypotension, jugular vein distention, muffled heart sounds
cards.rationale: Fluid in the pericardium compresses the heart → treat with pericardiocentesis.
cards.hint: Low BP, big necks, quiet heart.

cards.back: Pain, Pallor, Pulselessness, Paresthesia, Paralysis, Poikilothermia (cold)
cards.rationale: Arterial = the limb is cold, pale, pulseless; a surgical emergency.
Over-oxygenating can blunt the hypoxic drive; never withhold O₂ from a hypoxic client.

cards.back: Short-acting beta-agonist — albuterol (SABA)
cards.rationale: Steroid inhalers are controllers, not rescue; rinse mouth after steroids.

cards.front: Ominous sign in a severe asthma attack?
cards.back: A silent chest / absent wheezing
cards.rationale: No air movement means airflow has nearly stopped — respiratory failure.

cards.back: Sudden dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, tachycardia, anxiety
cards.rationale: Often follows DVT/immobility; give O₂, elevate HOB, anticoagulate.

cards.front: Continuous vigorous bubbling in the water-seal chamber means…?
cards.back: An air leak in the system
cards.rationale: Intermittent bubbling/tidaling is normal; continuous = check connections.

cards.back: Turns body fluids (urine, tears, sweat) orange
cards.rationale: Harmless but expected; can stain contact lenses. TB = airborne precautions.

cards.front: Causes of a falsely low pulse-ox reading?
cards.back: Cold/poor perfusion, movement, dark nail polish, low BP
cards.rationale: Correlate the number with how the client actually looks.

cards.back: IV fluids first → insulin → watch potassium closely
cards.rationale: Insulin drives potassium into cells; it can drop dangerously.

cards.back: 15 g fast-acting carbohydrate, recheck in 15 minutes
cards.rationale: Never give insulin; repeat if still low, then a protein/complex carb.

cards.back: Shaky, sweaty, tachycardic, hungry, confused/irritable
cards.rationale: Adrenergic + neuro symptoms; beta-blockers can mask them.

cards.front: Cushing’s vs Addison’s in one line?
cards.back: Cushing’s = everything HIGH (cortisol, glucose, weight, BP); Addison’s = everything LOW (BP, Na, glucose) with HIGH K
cards.rationale: Addisonian crisis = vascular collapse → fluids + hydrocortisone.

cards.back: Hypo = everything slow (cold, fatigue, weight gain); Hyper = everything fast (heat, weight loss, tachycardia)
cards.rationale: Thyroid storm (hyper crisis) = fever, tachycardia, agitation — emergency.

cards.back: SIADH = retain water → dilute (low) sodium, fluid restriction; DI = huge dilute urine → dehydration, high sodium
cards.rationale: SIADH = ‘Soaked Inside’; DI = ‘Dry Inside.’
